title: Speculative decoding: the best draft length
explain: Each extra draft token is kept only while the draft keeps matching (chance α), but each costs c of a target call. The curve is the paper's expected speedup for γ = 1…12; the dot is the best γ. Low α or expensive drafts push the curve under 1×: slower than plain decoding.

questions.q: Why not let the draft model guess 50 tokens at once?
questions.why: each extra guess is kept only while the draft keeps matching, and a long run almost never is

questions.q: What is c, and why does it matter so much?
questions.why: c is the cost of one draft token against one target call, so a pricey draft pulls the curve under the 1x line

questions.q: Can speculative decoding make generation slower?
questions.why: when acceptance is low or the draft is expensive, the best length is 1 and the speedup drops below 1

title: YaRN stretches only the slow RoPE dimensions
explain: NTK-by-parts: one bar per RoPE frequency, height = its wavelength. Fast dimensions (short bars) already cycle many times inside the training context and are left alone; slow ones (taller than the context line) are divided by s; the band in between is blended. Raise the scale s or the context L and watch the colors move.

questions.q: Why not divide every position by the same factor?
questions.why: the fast dimensions already fit the training context, and stretching them throws away position

questions.q: What does a wavelength longer than the context mean?
questions.why: that dimension has not finished one turn inside the training length, so it is the one to interpolate

questions.q: Which dimensions would break at a longer context?
questions.why: the tall bars, the slow ones, which the orange band divides by the scale

title: Mamba's Δ: remember, or reset to the new input
explain: The grey bars are inputs; orange ones are the tokens worth keeping. The blue line is the state h. Each step h ← e^(ΔA)·h + (1 − e^(ΔA))·x. A large Δ on orange tokens lets them overwrite h; a small Δ on the rest lets the noise slip past, so h holds on to the last orange value. Make the two Δ equal and the selection disappears.

questions.q: What does delta do to the hidden state?
questions.why: a large delta overwrites the state with the current input, and a small delta keeps what was already there

questions.q: How can one parameter both remember and forget?
questions.why: the same update mixes the old state and the new input, and delta picks the mix

questions.q: Why does delta have to depend on the input?
questions.why: the tokens worth keeping get a large delta and the noise gets a small one, which is the selection

title: SmoothQuant: hand the outliers from activations to weights
explain: Two activation channels carry huge outliers, so 8-bit rounding of X wipes out the small channels. Dividing channel j of X by s_j and multiplying row j of W by s_j leaves X·W exactly the same. α decides how much of the spike moves: at 0 X keeps it, at 1 W takes it, near 0.5 both are easy to quantize.

questions.q: Why are activations harder to quantize than weights?
questions.why: a few activation channels are huge, so 8-bit rounding wipes out the small ones

questions.q: Does rescaling change the layer output?
questions.why: dividing a channel of X and multiplying the matching row of W leaves the product the same

questions.q: Why is alpha 0.5 a good default?
questions.why: the error valley sits near the middle, where neither side keeps the whole spike

title: En el valle, el segundo momento frena el rebote
explain: Adam guarda dos momentos: hacia dónde empuja el gradiente y qué tan brusco es cada eje. En un valle angosto el segundo momento crece en la pared y achica ese paso. SGD, con el mismo lr, zigzaguea; si subes lr, se sale.

questions.q: ¿Por qué SGD rebota en un valle angosto y Adam no?
questions.why: el segundo momento achica el eje empinado

questions.q: ¿Qué se está promediando: la dirección o el tamaño del paso?
questions.why: los dos momentos, uno para cada cosa

questions.q: ¿Qué pasa si subo el lr y el valle sigue igual de angosto?
questions.why: SGD se sale y Adam aguanta más

title: La escala de la entrada no cruza el lote
explain: BatchNorm resta la media del lote y divide entre su desviación. Mueve la escala o el corrimiento de la entrada: la fila de arriba cambia y la del medio no. Gamma y beta, aprendidos, vuelven a estirar y a mover la salida.

questions.q: ¿Por qué la fila de en medio no se entera de la escala?
questions.why: restar la media y dividir cancela ese cambio

questions.q: ¿Para qué están gamma y beta si ya normalicé?
questions.why: la red todavía puede pedir otra escala

questions.q: ¿Qué se mueve cuando corro la entrada y qué se queda?
questions.why: solo la fila cruda; las otras usan el lote normalizado

title: La temperatura del maestro saca las chicas
explain: Subir la temperatura del maestro saca las probabilidades chicas, las que el argmax esconde. El alumno aprende de ese orden, no solo de la clase ganadora.

questions.q: ¿Por qué entrenar con las probabilidades del maestro?
questions.why: el orden entre las clases perdedoras también informa

questions.q: ¿Qué aparece cuando sube la temperatura?
questions.why: las probabilidades chicas se vuelven legibles

questions.q: ¿Qué se aplasta si la temperatura vuelve a uno?
questions.why: otra vez solo se ve la clase ganadora
